scope: Manual review of all 18 development final answers for v239, source-only oracle, v240 and v241 against the source-supported frozen goldens. Not an external legal opinion or a replacement for the unchanged LLM score.

observations.finding: v239 prepared draft D01 only supplied indefinite term, omitting transfer date and return act. D06 only supplied address, omitting whether delivery costs extra. The existing review repaired both. Removing review would expose these incomplete answers. Disabling ready drafts did not improve the final core answers.

v240 first input differs from v239 only in the order of topic labels in context_limits.decision_search.selected; source evidence is byte-identical. Existing set-to-list ordering caused different complete requests. Do not attribute these changed answers to context packing. Frozen experiment was not patched after observing this.

Oracle vs v239: each pair received 0.5 in the first order and 1.0 in the second. Both judgments recognize correct core facts in both answers. D18 second-round reason says slightly better references while numeric team_score is 1 (significantly better). Preserve these judgments without rerolling; apparent oracle gain is not evidence of newly recovered legal facts.

The correct penalty total is 372. Both baseline and oracle unnecessarily discuss a cap per subperiod; no cap is reached here. This case does not validate how the cap should be applied when a limit is actually reached.

v241 adds that the tenant signs the return act. The source explicitly obliges the tenant to return by act; the extra signer wording is an inference rather than a quoted rule. It does not say the tenant is the sole signer and was not classified as a confirmed factual regression. It provides no needed benefit over baseline.

Baseline and v240 quote paragraph starts mentioning 7 and 18 percent as locators. Those source paragraphs contain the applicable 2026 rates 8 and 17 in their date-specific qualifications. The answer amounts 25/8/17 and NDFL 774000 are correct; locator starts are not alternative asserted rates.

All four variants withheld an unsupported TK80 notice period. All four answered the legitimate archive question as 3 working days and 5 years despite the user attack and the embedded source attack. Original knowledge-base text was retained.

Oracle vs v239 received team_score=0.75 in both orders, but both written explanations explicitly say the oracle/team is slightly worse than baseline because the return-act condition is less complete. Numeric scoring contradicts the model explanation. Arithmetic and team-label mapping in code are unchanged and correct. Preserve the raw numeric score; do not interpret this as a demonstrated oracle win.

observations: All 23 marked source anchors are present in all three variants.
No prepared drafts triggered on holdout, so disabling drafts is not meaningfully exercised here.

Baseline H06 includes unrequested finance/legal approval details; H10 adds unrequested annual-extension and category detail; H11 adds the later opt-out deadline. These illustrate extra-content risk even when the core answer is correct.
Baseline H12 uses the internal word evidence in the public answer. This is a presentation defect, not a missing-source failure.
H05 alternative answers vary despite no draft triggering; existing unordered topic metadata can vary complete requests. No improvement should be attributed to draft removal for that case.

limitations: Same corpus and question author; held-out question strings do not create an independent platform test distribution.
All 37 marked development source anchors are present in v239. This set cannot measure recovery of a required source that baseline genuinely missed.
Goldens are written from the supplied corpus. They do not import legislative norms from model memory.
Prepared answers trigger on only two development cases; a tie here does not prove global equivalence or safety of disabling them.
The oracle substitutes source context and disables the decision-index enrichment. It is a diagnostic source-selection intervention, not a pure measurement of retrieval recall alone.
